To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the volume fluctuation effect is a major source of systematic uncertainty in the moment analysis, which is not taken into account in the experimental analyses and theoretical calculations; (2) auto-correlation effect is also an important source of systematic uncertainty; (3) statistical error of moment is not Gaussian distributed, and should be estimated using the bootstrap resampling method.
the moment analysis of the net-proton multipicity distribution is sensitive to volume fluctuation, auto-correlation, and the statistical errors in the data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the proper analysis and interpretation of experimental data on moments of conserved quantities in heavy-ion collisions and the comparison to the theoretical calculations of susceptibilities.
the proper use of net-proton distributions for extracting thermodynamic properties from heavy-ion collision experiments.
the systematic errors in the moments analysis of conserved quantity fluctuations in heavy-ion collisions and how to reduce these systematic effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the moments of net-proton distributions in Au + Au collisions at √SNN = 200 GeV at RHIC and Pb + Pb collisions at √Snn = 2.76 TeV at the LHC are not directly related to the thermodynamic volume fluctuations or auto-correlations of net-baryon distributions, as long as the volume of the system is large enough and the freeze-out temperature is not too low.

the moment analysis can be used to extract physical quantities, such as thermodynamic susceptibilities, provided the statistical errors are properly estimated and the effects of volume fluctuation and autocorrelation are properly taken into account.

the moments (σ2, S, κ) of net-proton multiplicities in heavy-ion collisions are not sensitive to the correlation volume of the system, but the moments of net-charge and/or net-baryon multiplicity are.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the moment analysis of the net-proton multipicity distribution is not a trivial task, but can be done properly with careful treatment of the volume fluctuation and the auto-correlation effects.
the moments of multiplicity distributions are not sensitive to the correlation lengths and the susceptibilities computed in Lattice QCD or Hadron Resonace Gas models.
the moments of net-proton distributions in heavy-ion collision are not only affected by the system volume but also by the auto-correlation between the net-protons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
one should be cautious in interpreting the results of moment analysis of net-charge or net-proton multipicity distributions, especially when the number of events is limited.
the volume fluctuations in net-proton multiplications distributions in heavy-ion collision can be reduced by considering the number of participants (Npart) in the event selection.
the moments of the multiplicity distributions should be extracted by taking into account the volume fluctuation and the auto-correlation effects.
